name: Dependent and Happy
editorial_article:
*Dependent and Happy* is a monumental work of minimal techno released in 2012 by the Chilean-German producer Ricardo Villalobos. Serving as his third solo studio album, the project emerged on the revered Berlin-based label Perlon, reflecting the label’s commitment to avant-garde electronic textures and extended, unconventional song structures. The album is famously expansive, originally issued across a multi-part, six-vinyl set that captured Villalobos at his most ambitious, weaving together intricate micro-house, glitch, and cerebral techno rhythms. The CD version, released in September 2012, offers a tighter, curated perspective on the work, mixed by Villalobos into a continuous flow that highlights the hypnotic, often disorienting nature of his production style.

Throughout the collection, Villalobos employs his signature technique of layering long, evolving sequences that favor texture and atmosphere over traditional club tropes. The track "Koito" serves as a landmark moment on the album, heavily sampling Atom Heart’s "(Holon) Slo Motion," while "Two Kids Set Off" integrates haunting archival audio related to the Columbine High School massacre, showcasing the artist's tendency to fold profound, often unsettling social commentary into immersive soundscapes. Collaborations with Max Loderbauer—notably on "Grumax" and "Die schwarze Massai"—further enrich the sonic palette, adding layers of analog warmth to the production. The album's deliberate lack of a digital release, paired with its complex physical rollout, underscores its status as an "outsider" house classic, cementing its place as a pivotal, if challenging, document of 2010s experimental electronic music. Its legacy persists as a testament to the power of the extended player to transport the listener through patience, precision, and profound sonic detail.
